primary_reviews.rationale: Consonantal collation places והמלך דוד זקן at the very head of oshb:1Kgs.1.1, and the syntax is as described for that clause: waw + definite subject + stative predicate זָקֵ֔ן, then the appositional בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים — no verb-first form, so a genuine disjunctive opening. The 1:5 pivot is equally real; וַאֲדֹנִיָּ֧ה בֶן חַגִּ֛ית fronts a fresh participant ahead of any finite verb, so the two disjunctives really do bracket the span. The closing evaluation is also correctly placed: oshb:1Kgs.1.4 ends וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א יְדָעָֽהּ, once more waw + subject + negated qatal, i.e. narratorial off-line comment rather than storyline. What does not survive checking is the aspectual generalisation. The cited verse does not lack wayyiqtol: 1:1 itself continues וַיְכַסֻּ֨הוּ֙ בַּבְּגָדִ֔ים, and 1:2-4 are a dense narrative chain — וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ, וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙, וַֽיִּמְצְא֗וּ, וַיָּבִ֥אוּ, וַתְּהִ֨י, וַתְּשָׁ֣רְתֵ֔הוּ. So the span is not 'durative background' as a whole; only its opening and closing clauses are off-line. The boundary itself is unharmed, since it rests on the two disjunctive frames, and high confidence is fairly priced.

challenges.claim: The parenthetical 'with no wayyiqtol (oshb:1Kgs.1.1)' and the follow-on 'setting durative background rather than event sequence' are false of the verse cited and of the span. oshb:1Kgs.1.1 contains וַיְכַסֻּ֨הוּ֙, and oshb:1Kgs.1.2-1Kgs.1.4 run six consecutive wayyiqtol forms (וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ, וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙, וַֽיִּמְצְא֗וּ, וַיָּבִ֥אוּ, וַתְּהִ֨י, וַתְּשָׁ֣רְתֵ֔הוּ).
challenges.suggested_action: Scope the grammatical claim to the clause: say the unit OPENS on a verbless/stative disjunctive (והמלך דוד זקן בא בימים) and CLOSES on another (והמלך לא ידעה), while 1:2-4 in between carry an ordinary wayyiqtol chain. Drop 'durative background' as a description of the whole span.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collated against oshb:1Kgs.1.1, the opening clause וְהַמֶּלֶךְ דָּוִד זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים is indeed verbless/disjunctive (waw + fronted subject + adjective), so the writer's contrast with wayyiqtol narration holds for that opening clause specifically, and the wayyiqtol וַיְכַסֻּהוּ that follows is background-scene machinery rather than plot advance. Web:1Kgs.1.4's closing evaluation matches the quoted 'the king didn't know her intimately' verbatim, and 1:5 does open on its own fronted-subject construction (וַאֲדֹנִיָּה בֶן חַגִּית מִתְנַשֵּׂא), so the seam the writer draws between senescence notice and usurpation narrative is real.

Machine collation of every Hebrew string in this row returns an exact consonantal match at the cited verse. The opening disjunctive והמלך דוד זקן בא בימים sits at oshb:1Kgs.1.1 and at no other verse in the book; the closing והמלך לא ידעה is likewise unique to oshb:1Kgs.1.4, so the frame the amendment now describes is real at both ends. I re-tallied the verb inventory independently rather than accepting the round-one list: oshb:1Kgs.1.1 carries וַיְכַסֻּהוּ; 1:2 has one wayyiqtol only (וַיֹּאמְרוּ — יְבַקְשׁוּ is jussive and וְעָמְדָה / וּתְהִי / וְשָׁכְבָה / וְחַם are weyiqtol-weqatal, rightly excluded); 1:3 has three (ויבקשו, וימצאו, ויבאו); 1:4 has two (ותהי, ותשרתהו). Six after 1:1, precisely as written. The row's ותהי is the 1:4 wayyiqtol and not the 1:2 homograph jussive, a distinction it gets right. The false 'no wayyiqtol' parenthetical and the span-wide durative characterization are both absent from the revised text, and the pivot participant ואדניה בן חגית is confirmed at oshb:1Kgs.1.5 only. No parashah claim is made and none is available in the single witness before 1Kgs.1.27.

OL-M8-1Kgs-001-1 challenged the claim that 1:1 carries no wayyiqtol and that 1:1-4 reads as durative background; the revision now scopes the disjunctive framing to the two verbless bookends alone (1:1's fronted והמלך דוד זקן בא בימים and 1:4's והמלך לא ידעה) and names the six interior wayyiqtols individually. I re-collated all six against oshb:1Kgs.1.2-4 (ויאמרו, ויבקשו, וימצאו, ויבאו, ותהי, ותשרתהו) and each form is present exactly as listed, so the count is not inflated or invented. No fresh quotation appears anywhere else in the row, the 1:5 pivot to Adonijah is described accurately, and the boundary itself is untouched by the correction. I found nothing else to press on here.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Pulled oshb:1Kgs.1.1 through 1.5 directly to re-derive the grammar rather than trust either primary's count. The disjunctive frame at the seams is genuine: 1:1 opens on the fronted stative זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים, 1:4 closes on the fronted וְהַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא יְדָעָהּ, and 1:5 opens its own fresh fronted subject וַאֲדֹנִיָּה בֶן חַגִּית. But OL-M8-1Kgs-001-1 is also right that 1:1's own second clause already carries a wayyiqtol (וַיְכַסֻּהוּ) and that 1:2-1:4 run six more in sequence (וַיֹּאמְרוּ, וַיְבַקְשׁוּ, וַיִּמְצְאוּ, וַיָּבִאוּ, וַתְּהִי, וַתְּשָׁרְתֵהוּ), so calling the whole span 'durative background... rather than event sequence' overstates what only the opening and closing clauses actually do. The frozen boundary itself rests on the two disjunctive frames, and neither of those depends on the overstated middle-verse claim, so the decision is unharmed.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every Hebrew string here lands where it is cited. oshb:1Kgs.1.5 reads וַאֲדֹנִיָּ֧ה בֶן חַגִּ֛ית מִתְנַשֵּׂ֥א לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י אֶמְלֹ֑ךְ, so the row's three morphological claims all hold at once: disjunctive waw plus fronted subject, a Hitpael participle מִתְנַשֵּׂא (durative self-elevation, not a punctual act), and the quoted 1cs yiqtol אֶמְלֹךְ introduced by לֵאמֹר. Nothing at 1:6-1:8 introduces a new speech frame or locale that would pre-empt the 1:10 stop, and the exclusion list of 1:10 is the negative counterpart of the invitation clause in the same verse. One trivial orthographic note without evidential weight: the row prints ואדניהּ with a mappiq in the final he, which the MT does not have; the consonantal text is identical, so no quote defect is recorded. The Hebrew at 1:5 and 1:9 checks out exactly as cited: מִתְנַשֵּׂא לֵאמֹר אֲנִי אֶמְלֹךְ opens the pretender's self-declaration, and וַיִּזְבַּח אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ at 1:9 is genuinely a fresh wayyiqtol clause, so the rejected 1:9 cut-point is a real candidate boundary and not a straw alternative. The writer's ground for keeping it inside the unit is defensible: the invitation roster at 1:9 (all his brothers, the king's sons, all the men of Judah) and the exclusion roster at 1:10 (Nathan, Benaiah, the mighty men, Solomon) parallel the adherent/non-adherent lists already opened at 1:7-8, so the feast completes an exposition begun at 1:5 rather than starting a new scene.

primary_reviews.rationale: ויאמר נתן אל בת־שבע is present verbatim (consonantally) at oshb:1Kgs.1.11, and it is a full speech formula with both participants named — the pairing is new to the book at that point, which is what gives the seam its force. The counter-proposal is rebutted on solid ground: oshb:1Kgs.1.15 opens וַתָּבֹ֨א בַת שֶׁ֥בַע אֶל הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ הַחַ֖דְרָה, a motion verb plus the locative he on הַחֶ֫דֶר, which is about as explicit a change of stage as Hebrew narrative provides. The internal reading of 1:11-14 as one uninterrupted directive also checks out: after the formula at 1:11 there is no further ויאמר until 1:15ff., so 1:12, 1:13 and 1:14 are continuation of the same quotation. The row's observation that 1:14's promise (הִנֵּ֗ה עוֹדָ֛ךְ מְדַבֶּ֥רֶת שָׁ֖ם עִם הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאֲנִי֙ אָב֣וֹא אַחֲרַ֔יִךְ) is the script for what follows is accurate as read.

The speech formula ויאמר נתן אל בת־שבע at oshb:1Kgs.1.11 and the scene break at 1:15 (ותבא בת־שבע אל־המלך החדרה) are both accurate, and the four-beat structure the writer names — report, counsel, scripted petition, promised entrance — matches the verse content of 1:11-14 exactly. One quotation is imprecise: the rationale presents 'while you are still talking there with the king, I will come in after you' in quotation marks as if verbatim, but web:1Kgs.1.14 actually reads 'Behold, while you are still talking there with the king, I will also come in after you and confirm your words' — the words 'also' and 'and confirm your words' are silently dropped.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale quotes web:1Kgs.1.14 as 'while you are still talking there with the king, I will come in after you' but the verse reads '...I will also come in after you and confirm your words' — the quotation silently truncates two elements while presented as a direct quote.
challenges.suggested_action: Either quote the full clause verbatim or mark the omission with an ellipsis; no change to the boundary itself is needed.

primary_reviews.rationale: LF-M8-1Kgs-003-1 asked that the truncated English quotation be completed or marked. web:1Kgs.1.14 reads 'while you are still talking there with the king, I will also come in after you and confirm your words', and the revised sentence now carries both restored elements — the adverb and the confirming clause — with no ellipsis needed. Turning to the Hebrew: ויאמר נתן אל בת שבע is a singleton in 1Kgs, found at oshb:1Kgs.1.11 alone, so the row's speech-formula opener is anchored where it says. The scene-edge string ותבא בת שבע אל המלך החדרה is equally unique to oshb:1Kgs.1.15, which is what the rejected alternative needs in order to treat 1:15 as a hard change of location and audience. The prior LF-M8-1Kgs-003-1 flag was a bare quotation trim: web:1Kgs.1.14 was cut before 'and confirm your words.' I looked past the repaired sentence for anything the surgery might have disturbed — the 1:11 and 1:15 Hebrew citations are unchanged and still verify against oshb, and the plan-hatching/execution boundary at 1:15 is argued on the same locative-entry formula as before, so nothing downstream depends on the trimmed phrase. This row reads clean.

primary_reviews.rationale: The mark handling is exactly right: pmarks_1Kgs.json carries 1Kgs.1.27 = SAMEKH, the row names it a setumah, discloses '(single-witness)', and explicitly restricts it to weak agreement with a boundary the discourse already fixes. The entry formula at oshb:1Kgs.1.15 is quoted correctly, and both halves of the echo really are in the text — oshb:1Kgs.1.22 והנה עודנה מדברת עם־המלך ונתן הנביא בא, oshb:1Kgs.1.14 עודך מדברת שם עם־המלך ואני אבוא אחריך. The trouble is the word 'verbatim'. Set the two side by side and three things differ: the 2fs suffix עוֹדָ֛ךְ becomes the 3fs עוֹדֶ֥נָּה, the deictic שָׁ֖ם of the plan drops out of the report, and Nathan's 1cs yiqtol אָב֣וֹא אַחֲרַ֔יִךְ is replaced by third-person וְנָתָ֥ן הַנָּבִ֖יא בָּֽא. That is a deliberate narratorial recasting, not a verbatim repetition — and the recasting is the better argument, because the person shift shows the narrator, not Nathan, binding the two entrances. The merge decision itself stands.

challenges.claim: 'fulfills the script verbatim' misdescribes the Hebrew. oshb:1Kgs.1.22 (וְהִנֵּ֛ה עוֹדֶ֥נָּה מְדַבֶּ֖רֶת עִם הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְנָתָ֥ן הַנָּבִ֖יא בָּֽא) differs from oshb:1Kgs.1.14 (הִנֵּ֗ה עוֹדָ֛ךְ מְדַבֶּ֥רֶת שָׁ֖ם עִם הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאֲנִי֙ אָב֣וֹא אַחֲרַ֔יִךְ) in person (עודך/עודנה), in the presence of שָׁם, and in the whole second clause (1cs promise vs 3ms narrated arrival).

primary_reviews.rationale: The intertextual echo claim is the load-bearing piece of this decision and it holds up: oshb:1Kgs.1.22's וְהִנֵּה עוֹדֶנָּה מְדַבֶּרֶת עִם הַמֶּלֶךְ וְנָתָן הַנָּבִיא בָּא does reuse the עודך/עודנה מדברת ... בוא vocabulary set up at 1:14, so Nathan's entrance really is depicted as the scripted fulfillment rather than an independent scene-opening arrival. The petition range (web:1Kgs.1.17-21) and the closing question at 1:27 are both correctly bounded, and the SAMEKH mark the writer cites after 1:27 does appear in pmarks_1Kgs.json, disclosed correctly as single-witness weak corroboration rather than a driver.

The substantive defect named by OL-M8-1Kgs-004-1 is repaired. 'Verbatim' is gone, and the row now itemizes the three real differences between the plan and its narration: person, the locative שם, and the whole second clause. Each is confirmed against the witness — oshb:1Kgs.1.14 runs הִנֵּה עוֹדָךְ מְדַבֶּרֶת שָׁם עִם הַמֶּלֶך וַאֲנִי אָבוֹא אַחֲרַיִךְ, oshb:1Kgs.1.22 runs וְהִנֵּה עוֹדֶנָּּה מְדַבֶּרֶת עִם הַמֶּלֶך וְנָתָן הַנָּבִיא בָּא. The strings ואני אבוא אחריך and והנה עודנה מדברת עם המלך ונתן הנביא בא each collate to their cited verse and to no other. The chamber-entry opener at oshb:1Kgs.1.15 is likewise clean, and the apparatus handling is correct: pmarks records SAMEKH at 1Kgs.1.27, the row types it setumah, tags it single-witness, and grants it only weak agreement with an edge the discourse already sets. What the repair broke is the pivot of its own argument. The row spells the 1:14 pronoun עודאך, with an aleph standing between dalet and final kaf. The Masoretic form is עוֹדָךְ, consonantally עודך; the string as printed matches nothing in 1Kgs and is not a Hebrew word. It occurs twice, once in the quotation and once inside the (עודאך→עודנה) arrow that is the amendment's whole point.

challenges.claim: The revised rationale quotes the 1:14 pronoun twice as עודאך (ayin-vav-dalet-aleph-final kaf). oshb:1Kgs.1.14 reads עוֹדָךְ, consonantal עודך; the aleph is spurious and the string as printed is absent from the book — the same class of defect as the dropped yod corrected at M8-1Kgs-025.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace both instances with עודך, in the prose quotation and in the (עודך→עודנה) pronoun-shift arrow. The person-shift argument is correct and needs no other change.

primary_reviews.rationale: OL-M8-1Kgs-004-1 objected to calling Nathan's 1:22 entrance a verbatim fulfillment of 1:14; the rewrite corrects this precisely, now stating outright that the recasting is 'not a verbatim fulfillment either,' and it walks through the actual differences — person shift עודך→עודנה, the dropped locative שם, and the swap from first-person pledge to third-person narration — all of which I confirmed against oshb:1Kgs.1.14 and 1.22 directly. But the repair introduced a fresh transcription fault of its own: the parenthetical renders 1:14's pronoun as עודאך, with an aleph that does not exist in the witness (oshb:1Kgs.1.14 has עודך, no aleph, and the pre-revision draft had it spelled correctly). This is a small orthographic slip rather than a substantive misreading — the surrounding argument about the pronoun shift still holds — but it is a citation error the reviewer is meant to catch.

challenges.claim: The parenthetical Hebrew gloss '(עודאך→עודנה)' misspells 1:14's pronoun with an inserted aleph; oshb:1Kgs.1.14 reads עודך (no aleph), and the pre-revision draft of this row had the correct spelling.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the transliteration to עודך→עודנה; no change to the argument or the boundary is needed.

The Hebrew of oshb:1Kgs.2.46 runs וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ ... וַיֵּצֵ֕א וַיִּפְגַּע בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת and then breaks off the chain: וְהַמַּמְלָכָ֥ה נָכ֖וֹנָה בְּיַד שְׁלֹמֹֽה is waw plus fronted subject plus predicate adjective, a disjunctive summary clause standing outside the wayyiqtol sequence, which is the opposite of the continuity the row asserts for it. primary_reviews.rationale: The restrictive-particle observation is exact. oshb:1Kgs.3.2 opens רַ֣ק הָעָ֔ם מְזַבְּחִ֖ים בַּבָּמ֑וֹת — רק plus fronted subject plus participle, genuinely durative and genuinely evaluative — and its causal tail כִּ֠י לֹא נִבְנָ֥ה בַ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה is quoted correctly. oshb:1Kgs.3.3 repeats the particle in the same evaluative key (רַ֚ק בַּבָּמ֔וֹת ה֥וּא מְזַבֵּ֖חַ וּמַקְטִֽיר), so two of the three verses really are narrator assessment. The petuchah handling is faultless: pmarks gives 1Kgs.3.2 = PE, the row names it, discloses it, calls its position mid-preface, and refuses it weight — this is the intended use of the weak tier. The contrast drawn against 3:4, however, is drawn too sharply. oshb:1Kgs.3.1 is not durative at all: it runs three consecutive wayyiqtol forms, וַיִּתְחַתֵּ֣ן שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה ... וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה וַיְבִיאֶ֨הָ֙ אֶל עִ֣יר דָּוִ֔ד, reporting discrete completed acts, and it is punctual in exactly the way the row says only 3:4 is. The preface reading survives on other grounds (no dialogue, no participant apparatus, an עַ֣ד־clause horizon reaching to the building programme), but the aspectual contrast as worded is wrong.

challenges.claim: '3:1-3 is durative, evaluative, and scene-less' is false of oshb:1Kgs.3.1, which is a three-link wayyiqtol chain (וַיִּתְחַתֵּ֣ן / וַיִּקַּ֣ח / וַיְבִיאֶ֨הָ֙) narrating punctual events — the same verb-first pattern the row attributes exclusively to 3:4 (וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ).
challenges.suggested_action: Confine the durative/evaluative description to 3:2-3 (the two רק clauses), and distinguish 3:1 as an annalistic notice that is punctual in form but carries no scene apparatus, participants in dialogue, or locale of action.

primary_reviews.rationale: The load-bearing morphological claim is right and is the best signal in the span: oshb:1Kgs.3.16 opens אָ֣ז תָּבֹ֗אנָה שְׁתַּ֛יִם נָשִׁ֥ים זֹנ֖וֹת אֶל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ — the particle אז governing a prefix form with past reference, an archaic construction the narrator reserves for marked openings, not the ordinary wayyiqtol. Calling it a fresh arrival formula is therefore justified on form as well as on content. The closing verse is described with unusual accuracy: oshb:1Kgs.3.28 does chain hearing, fearing and seeing (וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ כָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל ... וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י רָא֔וּ) and does end כִּ֥י חָכְמַ֧ת אֱלֹהִ֛ים בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ, so the summary is not a paraphrase but a reading of the ירא/ראה play in the verse. Both marks verify (1Kgs.3.23 = PE, 1Kgs.3.28 = SAMEKH), both are disclosed, and the petuchah that falls mid-scene after 3:23 is denied force outright — necessary here, since honouring it would have cut the king's restatement away from the sword test it introduces.

אָז תָּבֹאנָה really is an archaic narrative opener at oshb:1Kgs.3.16, matching the row's translation and framing, and the anecdote's internal sequence — testimony, restatement, sword test, self-revealing plea, verdict — tracks the verse content in order without gaps. The panoramic close at web:1Kgs.3.28 is quoted accurately and its thematic tie back to the 'understanding heart' Solomon requested at 3:9 is a fair, checkable link rather than an imposed reading. Both cited marks (PE after 3:23, SAMEKH after 3:28) are present in the marks file and correctly denied any driving force.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This row went unchallenged, and its two edge-claims both check out on inspection. oshb:1Kgs.3.16 opens with the marked archaic construction אָז תָּבֹאנָה rather than an ordinary wayyiqtol, which is real grammatical support for calling it a fresh-unit opener rather than a stylistic flourish. But two of the architectural descriptions misstate what the cited verses say: web:6.31 reads 'The lintel and door posts were a fifth part of the wall' and web:6.33 reads 'a fourth part of the wall' — both are fractional proportions (Hebrew חֲמִישִׁית / רְבִעִית, 'a fifth' / 'a fourth'), yet the row describes these as 'five-sided posts' and a 'four-sided nave doorway,' which asserts a polygonal shape the WEB witness text does not state.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale describes the doorposts of 6:31 and 6:33 as 'five-sided posts' and a 'four-sided nave doorway,' but web:1Kgs.6.31 and 6.33 state the posts were 'a fifth part of the wall' and 'a fourth part of the wall' respectively — a fractional proportion, not a count of sides.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise both phrases to reflect the fractional reading (e.g. 'doorposts sized to a fifth of the wall' / 'a fourth of the wall'); this is a descriptive correction only and does not affect the boundary, which rests on the 6:29 fronted-object clause and the 6:37 date-formula pivot.

primary_reviews.rationale: The architectural overreading is gone and what replaced it follows the cited witnesses. web:1Kgs.6.31 has 'a fifth part of the wall' and web:1Kgs.6.33 'out of a fourth part of the wall'; the row now uses that wording and additionally flags חמשית and רבעית as disputed ordinals, taking both remedies OL-M8-1Kgs-031-1 offered. Each ordinal collates to its cited verse and appears nowhere else in the book. The fronted-object opener ואת כל קירות הבית is unique to oshb:1Kgs.6.29; the gilded floor of 6:30, the olive-wood and cypress leaves of 6:31-34, and the three-courses-plus-cedar court of 6:36 all check out; and no parashah claim is made for a span where the single witness records none (pmarks is empty between 1Kgs.6.13 and 1Kgs.7.12). One descriptor does not survive collation. The row calls 6:29-36 'one asyndetic register', but every constituent clause is waw-initial: ואת (29), ואת (30), ואת (31), ושתי (32), וכן (33), ושתי (34), וקלע (35), ויבן (36). Asyndeton means the absence of the conjunction; what is actually there is syndetic parataxis, which supports the row's 'one sweep' reading just as well under an accurate name.

challenges.claim: 'a close-out sweep in one asyndetic register' misnames the syntax. Every clause in oshb:1Kgs.6.29-36 begins with waw (ואת, ואת, ואת, ושתי, וכן, ושתי, וקלע, ויבן), so the series is syndetic, not asyndetic. The same descriptor recurs at M8-1Kgs-033 ('chained asyndetically' of 7:2-8, which are likewise all waw-initial).
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'asyndetic register' with an accurate term — 'one waw-chained register of fronted-object clauses', or the 'simple parataxis' wording already used at M8-1Kgs-050 — and fix the parallel phrase in M8-1Kgs-033. The one-sweep argument is unaffected.

primary_reviews.rationale: Fractional wall proportions had been rewritten as physical door-post counts, and reviewers on both sides caught it (LF-M8-1Kgs-031-1, OL-M8-1Kgs-031-1). Checking web:1Kgs.6.31 and 6.33 directly, WEB gives 'a fifth part of the wall' and 'a fourth part of the wall,' language the row now reproduces instead of inventing 'five-sided' and 'four-sided' posts, and it labels the underlying ordinals חמשית and רבעית as 'disputed' rather than asserting a settled sense for them — the more cautious framing that was asked for. Re-reading 6:29-36 in sequence, the carving, gilding, and inner-court items still track spatially outward as the row claims.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: LF-M8-1Kgs-031-1 and OL-M8-1Kgs-031-1 converge on one shared defect, and web:1Kgs.6.31 together with web:1Kgs.6.33 settles it directly: the verses read 'a fifth part of the wall' and 'out of a fourth part of the wall,' fractional measures, not the row's 'five-sided posts' and 'four-sided nave doorway.' The underlying Hebrew terms חֲמִשִׁית and רְבִעִית are ordinals of disputed architectural sense, which OL rightly flags as leaving room for a polygonal construal in principle — but that construal is not what either witness cited in the row actually states, so citing web:6.31/6.33 for a shape-count is unsupported regardless of which reading is eventually preferred. Because both primaries converge on the identical citation-versus-content gap, I reconcile to a single remedy: follow the cited WEB wording ('a fifth part' / 'a fourth part of the wall'), and if the polygonal reading is wanted elsewhere in the draft, mark it explicitly as one construal of the disputed חמשית/רבעית rather than presenting it as the witnesses' own statement. The spatial close-out argument for the 6:29-36 boundary, resting on the fronted-object clause at 6:29 and the date-formula pivot at 6:37, is unaffected.

primary_reviews.rationale: The envelope argument is sound and checkable. בשנה הרביעית occurs in exactly two verses in the book, oshb:1Kgs.6.1 and oshb:1Kgs.6.37, so the colophon really does reach back to the era formula; the month name matches too, though the noun differs (בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ זִ֗ו at 6:1, בְּיֶ֖רַח זִֽו at 6:37), which if anything sharpens the point that 6:37 is a deliberate reprise rather than a continuation. The forward contrast is also exact: oshb:1Kgs.7.1 opens וְאֶת בֵּיתוֹ֙ בָּנָ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה, object marker fronted before the qatal, with שְׁלֹ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה as its own figure against the seven years of 6:38. The error is in the grammatical label. Neither date sentence is verbless: oshb:1Kgs.6.37 has the Pual perfect יֻסַּ֖ד ('was founded'), and oshb:1Kgs.6.38 has both כָּלָ֣ה הַבַּ֔יִת and the wayyiqtol וַיִּבְנֵ֖הוּ. What is distinctive about these two verses is fronted temporal phrases and passive/impersonal predication, not the absence of a verb.

challenges.claim: 'two verbless date sentences' is false of both verses. oshb:1Kgs.6.37 contains the finite Pual יֻסַּ֖ד בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה; oshb:1Kgs.6.38 contains כָּלָ֣ה הַבַּ֔יִת and the wayyiqtol וַיִּבְנֵ֖הוּ שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'verbless date sentences' with an accurate description — two date-fronted notices with passive/impersonal predicates (יֻסַּד, כָּלָה) and a closing summary wayyiqtol — which still supports the annalistic-colophon reading.

primary_reviews.rationale: The envelope argument in this row is sound and independently verifiable: 6:37's 'fourth year... month Ziv' does reprise 6:1's date coordinates exactly, and 7:1's fronted-object contrast ואת־ביתו בנה שלמה with its thirteen-year figure is quoted accurately. But the description of 6:37-38 as 'two verbless date sentences' doesn't match the grammar: oshb:6.37 has the finite passive verb יֻסַּד ('was founded'), and oshb:6.38 has both כָּלָה ('was finished') and the wayyiqtol וַיִּבְנֵהוּ ('and he built it') — neither verse is verbless, even though both are clearly outside the specification-catalogue's asyndetic style.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale calls 6:37-38 'two verbless date sentences,' but oshb:1Kgs.6.37 contains the finite verb יֻסַּד and oshb:1Kgs.6.38 contains כָּלָה and the wayyiqtol וַיִּבְנֵהוּ — neither verse lacks a verb.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'verbless' with a description matching the actual grammar, e.g. 'annalistic date notices standing outside the specification's asyndetic register' — the envelope/bracket argument itself does not depend on the verses being verbless and needs no other change.

primary_reviews.rationale: 'Verbless' is gone and its replacement is morphologically accurate at both verses. oshb:1Kgs.6.37 fronts בַּשָׁנָה הָרְבִיעִית before the Pual יֻסַּד, and oshb:1Kgs.6.38 fronts וּבַשָּׁנָה הָאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה before כָּלָה הַבַּיִת and closes with the summary wayyiqtol וַיִּבְנֵהוּ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים. All three quoted strings match only their cited verses, and 'passive and impersonal predicates ... plus a closing wayyiqtol' is a fair description of יסד and כלה as pointed. The envelope claim also holds on inspection rather than assertion: oshb:1Kgs.6.1 carries בַּשָׁנָה הָרְבִיעִית with the month Ziv, so year and month do bracket the account, the only difference being בְּחֹדֶשׁ at 6:1 against בְּיֶרַח at 6:37, which the row does not misreport. The pivot quotation ואת ביתו בנה שלמה is confirmed at oshb:1Kgs.7.1. No apparatus claim is made anywhere in this two-verse row.

A grammatical description had outrun the evidence: 'verbless date sentences' for two verses that each contain a finite verb, a fault the sonnet-side and opus-side reviewers spotted independently (LF-M8-1Kgs-032-1, OL-M8-1Kgs-032-1). Pulling oshb:1Kgs.6.37-38 to check the replacement wording — 'date-fronted notices carrying passive and impersonal predicates' — against the actual forms, the passive יסד, the stative כלה, and the closing wayyiqtol ויבנהו are all present exactly where the row now says they are. The 6:1/6:37 date-envelope argument tying the fourth-year Ziv notice back to the temple's start is untouched by the correction and still holds against oshb:1Kgs.6.1.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: LF-M8-1Kgs-032-1 and OL-M8-1Kgs-032-1 catch the identical grammatical mislabel, and parsing oshb:1Kgs.6.37 and oshb:1Kgs.6.38 verb by verb confirms it: 6:37 carries the finite Pual יֻסַּד ('was founded') and 6:38 carries both כָּלָה ('was finished') and the closing wayyiqtol וַיִּבְנֵהוּ ('and he built it') — neither verse is verbless. What actually distinguishes these two verses from the surrounding specification is fronted temporal phrases with passive or impersonal predication, not an absence of verbs. Since both primaries independently name the same fix, I reconcile to OL's more explicit phrasing, which names the actual predicates rather than sidestepping them: replace 'two verbless date sentences' with 'two date-fronted notices built on passive or impersonal predicates (יֻסַּד, כָּלָה), closing on a summary wayyiqtol.' The reprise of 6:1's date coordinates and the envelope argument for the colophon boundary do not depend on verblessness and are untouched.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opener is transcribed accurately and analysed accurately: oshb:1Kgs.7.1 reads וְאֶת בֵּיתוֹ֙ בָּנָ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה שְׁלֹ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה, object marker fronted before the qatal, in pointed contrast with the temple's seven years — and the petuchah after 7:12 verifies as PE in pmarks, is disclosed, and is correctly subordinated to the summons formula at 7:13. The masonry close is also better attested than the row claims: oshb:1Kgs.7.12 does not merely echo 6:36, it names it (וְלַחֲצַ֧ר בֵּית יְהוָ֛ה הַפְּנִימִ֖ית), which is a genuine cross-tie. The problem is the rejection argument. oshb:1Kgs.7.6 opens וְאֵ֨ת אוּלָ֤ם הָֽעַמּוּדִים֙ עָשָׂ֔ה and oshb:1Kgs.7.7 opens וְאוּלָ֤ם הַכִּסֵּא֙ ... עָשָׂ֑ה — both are waw plus fronted object plus qatal, the identical construction the row treats as unique to 7:1, and oshb:1Kgs.7.8 fronts a subject phrase (וּבֵיתוֹ֩ אֲשֶׁר יֵ֨שֶׁב שָׁ֜ם) in the same style. Three further clause-initial framing formulas therefore sit inside the span. The merge can still be defended — none of those entries carries a completion formula, and the כָּל אֵ֜לֶּה summary of oshb:1Kgs.7.9 gathers them all — but the reason as written is false and the alternative is stronger than the row concedes.

challenges.claim: 'only 7:1 carries a clause-initial framing formula' is false. oshb:1Kgs.7.6 (וְאֵ֨ת אוּלָ֤ם הָֽעַמּוּדִים֙ עָשָׂ֔ה) and oshb:1Kgs.7.7 (וְאוּלָ֤ם הַכִּסֵּא֙ ... עָשָׂ֑ה) use the same waw + fronted-object + qatal frame as 7:1, and oshb:1Kgs.7.8 fronts וּבֵיתוֹ֩ אֲשֶׁר יֵ֨שֶׁב שָׁ֜ם before הָיָ֑ה.
challenges.suggested_action: Rebuild the rejection on grounds that survive: no entry inside 7:2-8 carries a completion or closure formula, the entries are asyndetically chained without participant or temporal change, and oshb:1Kgs.7.9 gathers them under כָּל אֵלֶּה so the masonry summary presupposes the whole set. Acknowledge the repeated fronted-object frames rather than denying them.

primary_reviews.rationale: The palace-dossier content is accurately reported end to end — the fronted-object opener at 7:1, the named buildings of 7:2-8, and the masonry summary of 7:9-12 whose 'all these' language really does generalize across the whole complex (כָּל אֵלֶּה at oshb:7.9) — and the claimed echo between 7:12's cedar-and-stone course description and 6:36's inner court is close to verbatim in Hebrew, a genuine catch. But the rejected-alternative's specific grammatical claim doesn't hold: it says 'only 7:1 carries a clause-initial framing formula,' yet oshb:7.6 (וְאֵת אוּלָם הָעַמּוּדִים עָשָׂה), 7.7 (וְאוּלָם הַכִּסֵּא...עָשָׂה), and 7.8 (וּבֵיתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יֵשֶׁב שָׁם...) all front their object or subject before the verb exactly as 7:1 does — three more instances of the same construction the sentence claims is unique to the opening verse.

challenges.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative states 'only 7:1 carries a clause-initial framing formula,' but oshb:1Kgs.7.6, 7.7, and 7.8 all use the same fronted-object/subject construction before the verb that 7:1 uses — the uniqueness claim is factually incorrect.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop or revise the 'only 7:1' claim; the argument for keeping the buildings in one row is already sufficiently carried by the 7:9-12 masonry note's explicit 'all these' generalization, which doesn't need this overstated grammatical support.

primary_reviews.rationale: The uniqueness claim has been abandoned in favour of what the text actually shows, and all three replacement grounds hold under collation. oshb:1Kgs.7.6 is וְאֵת אוּלָם הָעַמּוּדִים עָשָׂה, oshb:1Kgs.7.7 is וְאוּלָם הַכִּסֵּא אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁפָּט שָׁם ... עָשָׂה, and oshb:1Kgs.7.8 fronts וּבֵיתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יֵשֶׁב שָׁם before הָיָה — each quoted with the right consonants and each matching its cited verse alone, so the concession about repeated fronted-object frames is exact rather than approximate. I tested the load-bearing replacement claim deterministically: searching 7:2-8 for the roots תמם, כלה and שלם returns nothing in any of those seven verses, against וַתִּתֹּם מְלֶאכֶת הָעַמּוּדִים at oshb:1Kgs.7.22 and כָּזֹאת עָשָׂה at 7:37, so 'no entry carries its own closure formula' is verified, not merely plausible. כל אלה is unique to oshb:1Kgs.7.9, and the PE after 1Kgs.7.12 is typed and disclosed. The single wording I cannot certify is 'chained asyndetically': 7:2-8 open ויבן, וספן, ושקפים, וכל, ואת, ואולם, וביתו — a conjunction on every clause.

challenges.claim: 'the buildings are chained asyndetically' is contradicted by the witness: oshb:1Kgs.7.2-8 each begin with a waw (ויבן, וספן, ושקפים, וכל, ואת, ואולם, וביתו). The chaining is syndetic. The wording entered the row from the round-one suggested action and is inaccurate there too.
challenges.suggested_action: Say 'chained by simple waw parataxis' (the phrasing already used in M8-1Kgs-050) instead of 'asyndetically'. The two other grounds — absence of entry-closers in 7:2-8 and the כל אלה gathering at 7:9 — are verified and carry the merge on their own.

primary_reviews.rationale: The uniqueness claim underneath this row's rejected alternative did not survive contact with the text — 7:6, 7:7, and 7:8 all open with the same fronted-object-plus-verb pattern the row had credited to 7:1 alone, a point LF-M8-1Kgs-033-1 and OL-M8-1Kgs-033-1 each demonstrated from opposite ends of the review. The rejection is rebuilt on sturdier ground now: no completion or closure formula appears anywhere in 7:2-8 (contrast ותתם at 7:22), the buildings are chained without any change of participant or time reference, and כל אלה at 7:9 gathers the whole set for one masonry summary. I confirmed the repeated fronted frames against oshb myself, and the row now states them openly instead of denying them.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: LF-M8-1Kgs-033-1 and OL-M8-1Kgs-033-1 both dispute the same sentence, and pulling all four candidate verses confirms the challenge: oshb:1Kgs.7.2 is a plain wayyiqtol (וַיִּבֶן), but oshb:1Kgs.7.6 opens וְאֵת אוּלָם הָעַמּוּדִים עָשָׂה, oshb:1Kgs.7.7 opens וְאוּלָם הַכִּסֵּא...עָשָׂה, and oshb:1Kgs.7.8 opens וּבֵיתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יֵשֶׁב שָׁם...הָיָה — three more instances of the exact fronted-object-or-subject-plus-verb pattern the rationale calls unique to 7:1. 'Only 7:1 carries a clause-initial framing formula' is simply false of the span. Since both primaries name the identical fix, I reconcile to one remedy, and OL's version is the more complete of the two: rebuild the rejection on the grounds that actually hold — no entry in 7:2-8 carries its own completion formula, the entries chain asyndetically with no participant or temporal break, and oshb:1Kgs.7.9's כָּל אֵלֶּה gathers the whole set under one masonry summary. LF's simpler suggestion (drop the claim and rest on the 7:9 'all these' language alone) is a valid fallback but leaves the stronger asyndetic-chaining argument unstated. Ruling SUPPORTED for both; the row's boundary is untouched either way.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both Hebrew fragments come back clean: וישלח המלך שלמה ויקח את־חירם מצר at oshb:1Kgs.7.13, and ותתם מלאכת העמודים closing oshb:1Kgs.7.22; the latter deserves the weight the row puts on it, since וַתִּתֹּ֖ם is a Qal wayyiqtol of תמם with מְלֶאכֶת as subject, a genuine terminative clause of a kind that occurs nowhere else in the bronze catalogue. The Bezalel comparison is grounded rather than decorative: oshb:1Kgs.7.14 has וַ֠יִּמָּלֵא אֶת הַחָכְמָ֤ה וְאֶת הַתְּבוּנָה֙ וְאֶת הַדַּ֔עַת לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כָּל מְלָאכָ֖ה בַּנְּחֹ֑שֶׁת, the same triad of endowment nouns plus an infinitival purpose clause. The refusal to strip 7:13-14 into a two-verse header is well argued from the same verse: it ends וַיָּבוֹא֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת כָּל מְלַאכְתּֽוֹ, establishing Hiram as the subject that 7:15's fabrication verbs simply continue.

The summons formula וישלח המלך שלמה ויקח את־חירם מצר at oshb:7.13 and Hiram's endowment notice at web:7.14 both match the source, and the argument for keeping the artisan introduction with the pillar entry is directly verifiable: web:7.14 ends with Hiram as the subject who 'performed all his work,' and 7:15's fashioning verb continues that same unstated subject with no new frame. The completion formula ותתם מלאכת העמודים closing the entry at oshb:7.22 is quoted exactly.

primary_reviews.rationale: ויעש את־הים מוצק heads oshb:1Kgs.7.23 as quoted. The row's structural principle — that this catalogue individuates its entries by ויעש plus a named object — is checkable and holds at each of the three verses named: 7:23 (הַיָּם), 7:27 (הַמְּכֹנוֹת), 7:38 (עֲשָׂרָה כִיֹּרוֹת). That is a document-internal criterion rather than a thematic one, which is why the functional bundling of sea with bases deserves the rejection it gets. For 7:26 the apparatus yields a petuchah, single-witness as stated, and the row places it at an end the ויעש formula of 7:27 independently establishes — mark following argument, not leading it. Content checks against the cited verses: brim-to-brim ten cubits with a thirty-cubit circumference at 7:23, the oxen in four triads facing outward with hindquarters inward at 7:25, and the handbreadth thickness, lily brim and two-thousand-bath capacity at 7:26.

Every measurement this row lists for the molten sea — ten cubits brim to brim, the thirty-cubit encircling line, twelve oxen at three per compass point with hindquarters inward, and the two-thousand-bath capacity — matches web:7.23-26 precisely, including the oxen arrangement, which I counted directly rather than assuming. The claim that entries are individuated by a ויעש-plus-object formula (sea, bases, basins) is independently confirmed by the parallel openings at oshb:7.27 and 7.38, both reviewed under decision 036.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: No challenge landed here. The measurements given for the sea — ten cubits brim to brim, the thirty-cubit line, the oxen in triads at the four points — match the cited verses. No modification needed.

The אז יקהל opener at oshb:8.1 is quoted accurately, and its grammatical parallel to 3:16's אז תבאנה is real and precisely stated — both are אז-plus-yiqtol archaic preterite constructions, and the row is careful not to overextend that specific claim to 8:12's אז אמר, which is actually אז-plus-qatal, a different construction the row correctly avoids conflating with the first. Treating 8:14 as a turn inside one speech-event, not as the head of a fresh row, is defensible on the Hebrew — סבב plus פנים is a stage direction, not a speech formula, and no new speaker is introduced anywhere between 8:12 and 8:21. The blessing incipit is where the row says: ברוך יהוה occurs four times in the book (1:48, MT 5:21, 8:15, 8:56) and 8:15 is one of them. The poetic couplet at web:8.12-13 and the stage-direction pivot ויסב המלך את־פניו at oshb:8.14 are both quoted faithfully, and the claim that this is one continuous speech-event rather than two acts is supported by the text itself — no new speaker or scene intervenes, only a change of addressee direction. The Davidic retrospective content (election of David, his thwarted intent, the son-shall-build oracle, and the fulfillment claim) tracks web:8.15-21 in order, and I confirmed forward that 8:22's altar-standing posture, cited as the next unit's opener, is exactly what the following verse describes.

At oshb:1Kgs.8.32, 8.34, 8.36, 8.39 and 8.43 the text has (וְ)אַתָּ֣ה תִּשְׁמַ֣ע הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם — an independent pronoun plus a 2ms yiqtol, not a weqatal. primary_reviews.rationale: The posture-formula envelope framing this whole prayer is solid — oshb:8.22's ויעמד...ויפרש כפיו opens it and the dismount at 8:54 (reviewed under decision 042) closes it — and the sevenfold count of petition cases (oath, defeat, drought, famine/siege, foreigner, battle, captivity) is accurate against the text. Two smaller claims don't hold up on inspection, though. First, the cited refrain form ושמעת השמים doesn't match five of the seven verses it's attached to: 8:32, 8:34, 8:36, and 8:39 all read ואתה תשמע השמים (a different construction with the independent pronoun), and only 8:45 and 8:49 actually use ושמעת. primary_reviews.rationale: ויהי ככלות שלמה להתפלל opens oshb:1Kgs.8.54 exactly as quoted, and the row's reading of that verse as a formal hinge is stronger than it claims: the verse does not merely announce that the prayer is over, it physically reverses 8:22 — קָ֞ם מִלִּפְנֵ֨י מִזְבַּ֤ח יְהוָה֙ מִכְּרֹ֣עַ עַל בִּרְכָּ֔יו, rising from kneeling before the same altar he had stood before. The completion formula ויהי ככלות שלמה להתפלל genuinely opens this unit at oshb:8.54, and the posture reversal it describes is directly supported by the verse itself, which specifies the king rose 'from kneeling on his knees' — new information not stated at 8:22, but not a contradiction the row needs to resolve. The forward argument is solid: oshb:1Kgs.9.24 does open with the restrictive particle אַ֣ךְ and a different subject entirely (בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה), so the corvée document is complete at the officer count. One point the row could press harder: the 550 officers of web:1Kgs.9.23 do not simply repeat the 3,300 of web:1Kgs.5.16 (= oshb:1Kgs.5.30) but stand in tension with it, so 'answers' is doing softer work than the numbers warrant — it is a cross-reference, not a reconciliation, and the row does not claim otherwise.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL-M8-1Kgs-056-1 is the only challenge here, and comparing the two verses directly confirms it: oshb:1Kgs.11.26 ends וַיָּרֶם יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ, a wayyiqtol, while the Hiphil perfect הֵרִים יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ that the row's composite quotation attributes to 11:26 actually sits inside 11:27's relative clause, וְזֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר הֵרִים יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ. The internal argument for keeping the panel-head with the Ahijah scene — that 11:26-28 narrates no event of its own — is unaffected and independently checkable: oshb:1Kgs.11.26-28 contains characterization and motive but no depicted act of rebellion beyond the hand-raising notice itself.

Every beat of the Shechem negotiation — the movement formula, the three-day adjournment, both counsel rounds with the scorpions line quoted identically at 12:11 and 12:14, the fulfillment aside at 12:15, and the secession cry — matches web:12.1-19 in sequence and without distortion. The account's internal sequence matches the cited verses point for point: the interior monologue at web:1Kgs.12.26-27, the acclamation הִנֵּה אֱלֹהֶיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל at 12:28, the Bethel/Dan placement at 12:29, the verdict clause at 12:30, the improvised priesthood at 12:31, and the eighth-month feast at 12:32-33 — a feast the text explicitly calls self-invented (אֲשֶׁר בָּדָא מִלִּבּוֹ). The petuchah after 12:33 matches pmarks as PE, is labelled single-witness, and is granted no more than agreement. The rejection is well grounded in the Hebrew of the next verse: oshb:1Kgs.13.1 opens with וְהִנֵּה plus a new principal and then re-sets Jeroboam as a circumstantial clause (וְיָרָבְעָ֛ם עֹמֵ֥ד עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ), which is scene-opening machinery rather than continuation.

But the correspondence claimed between the two speeches is overstated. oshb:1Kgs.20.23 has אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָרִים֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם with the proposed remedy בַּמִּישׁ֔וֹר, while the oracle at oshb:1Kgs.20.28 has אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָרִים֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹֽא אֱלֹהֵ֥י עֲמָקִ֖ים ה֑וּא. primary_reviews.rationale: The prophet's return warning and the Syrian servants' hills-god strategy session, including the kings-for-captains and horse-for-horse reorganization, both match web:20.22-25 exactly, and both cited marks are genuine. primary_reviews.rationale: 'Verbatim' has given way to a description of quotation-with-substitution, and the substitution is precisely what the two verses do. אֱלֹהֵי הָרִים is the only material they share, occurring at oshb:1Kgs.20.23 and oshb:1Kgs.20.28 and at no third verse in the book. 20:23 reads אֱלֹהֵי הָרִים אֱלֹהֵיהֶם and proposes fighting בַּמִּישׁוֹר; 20:28 reads אֱלֹהֵי הָרִים יְהוָה וְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי עֲמָקִים הוּא. So יהוה displaces אלהיהם and עמקים displaces מישור, as the row says; עמקים is confined to 20:28 and במישור to 20:23 and 20:25. The council opener ויגש הנביא אל מלך ישראל is unique to oshb:1Kgs.20.22, and the return-of-the-year hinge at 20:26 is where the row places it. Both apparatus citations are accurate and both are qualified: SAMEKH after 1Kgs.20.22 typed as setumah, PE after 1Kgs.20.25 typed as petuchah, each described as articulating or seconding an edge it does not create.

The word 'verbatim' had been doing more work than the Hebrew supports, a call made independently by LF-M8-1Kgs-092-1 and echoed by OL-M8-1Kgs-092-1. The row now describes 'quotation-with-substitution': the epithet אלהי הרים repeats, but יהוה replaces the Syrians' אלהיהם and עמקים replaces their במישור. Setting oshb:1Kgs.20.23 and 20.28 side by side confirms exactly this pattern — same opening phrase, different subject, different antonym — so the new description is more accurate than 'verbatim' ever was, and the symmetrical-council-pair reading it supports still holds without needing lexical identity.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: LF-M8-1Kgs-092-1 and OL-M8-1Kgs-092-1 each dispute the identical 'verbatim' claim, and setting oshb:1Kgs.20.23 beside oshb:1Kgs.20.28 settles the matter for both: the only material genuinely shared is the two-word epithet אלהי הרים. 20:23 continues אֱלֹהֵיהֶם (their god) ... בַּמִּישׁוֹר (in the plain), while 20:28 continues יְהוָה (naming Yahweh explicitly) ... וְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי עֲמָקִים הוּא (not a god of the valleys) — a different subject and a different antonym term, not lexical identity. Since both primaries converge on the same finding, I reconcile to a single remedy, favoring OL's fuller phrasing over LF's simpler substitution because it names what actually changes: the oracle quotes אלהי הרים back at the Syrians while substituting יהוה for אלהיהם and עמקים for מישור, turning a tactical claim into a theological one. Ruling SUPPORTED for both. The symmetrical-council-pair argument for keeping 20:22-25 together — each side reading the last engagement and planning the next, with the return-of-the-year formula at 20:26 delivering what both anticipate — does not depend on lexical identity and is unaffected.
